audit.whatIsWrong: Facebreaker is described as a pull-stun in eight places — spikes[1], early, mid, wants.you[1], wants.foe[0], whys[2], dontsFull[2] and the report row built from it. Its actual condition is never stated.
audit.why: Riot's Facebreaker text: "Sett pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him, dealing damage and stunning them. If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned." In a solo lane against one champion it is a SLOW by default. It only stuns when Sett has enemies on both sides of him, which in practice means you on one side and a minion on the other. That converts the most feared ability in the matchup into something the reader controls with their feet: keep the wave off his far side and the pull cannot hold you for the Haymaker. Told only that it stuns, a reader plays the entire lane out of a 490-range circle for no reason, and still gets stunned because they never learned what causes it.
audit.corrected: The both-sides condition written into spikes[1], early, mid, wants.you[1], wants.foe[0], whys[2], breakdown.cooldowns, dontsFull[2] and report[5], with the real 16s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Haymaker is described as "% true damage" that "cracks through your armor", and wants.you[2] tells the reader to "sidestep the aimed Haymaker cone — it's a directional smash, not a zone". The part that matters is missing and one detail is invented.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Sett passively stores damage he takes as Grit. On cast, Sett expends all stored Grit to gain a shield and punch an area, dealing true damage in the center and physical damage on the sides." There is no percentage in it. And it is not sidestep-or-eat-it: the sides of the punch still hit you, they just hit for physical instead of true. So the instruction is not "dodge the cone", it is "do not be in the middle of it" — which is a much smaller and much more achievable movement. The shield is also the reason _missing-interactions.json flags this matchup for shield-absorbs-burst, and it is the reason feeding Grit is self-defeating.
audit.corrected: Centre-versus-sides written into wants.you[2], late, dosFull[1], dontsFull[1], breakdown.cooldowns and report[5]; the unsupported percentage removed; the shield tied to the Grit you personally put into the bar.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three effects are attributed to abilities that do not have them. mid and wants.foe[1] credit Sett with "lifesteal sustain"; spikes[2] says The Show Stopper deals "bonus-HP damage"; late calls him a "grab-and-suppress threat".
audit.why: Pit Grit gives "additional health regeneration based off of his missing health" — regeneration, not lifesteal, which matters because it works out of combat and cannot be reduced by hitting him less. The Show Stopper's text is "carries an enemy champion through the air and slams them into the ground, dealing damage and slowing all enemies near where they land" — no bonus-HP scaling and no suppression anywhere in it.
audit.corrected: Lifesteal replaced with missing-health regen, the bonus-HP claim dropped, and the suppress claim removed. Show Stopper restated with its real 400 range and 120s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: late and whys[6] credit "the flat armor pen from your R passive" / "R armor pen", and early and wants.you[0] call the empowered auto a "Medarda-empowered auto".
audit.why: Public Execution has no armour penetration — it blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line, suppresses, then slams for damage and a stun. And "Medarda Maxim" is not an ability; Ambessa's only passive is Drakehound's Step. Against Sett the invented penetration is specifically misleading, because the entry uses it as the reason the first-item burst works against a champion whose defining defensive tool is a shield rather than armour.
audit.corrected: Both replaced with the real names and the real reason short trades work — Grit has not filled yet.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart disagrees with its own whys[] at four of seven stages, and the lane is rated EVEN 6/10 at a 46.24% win rate over 519 games. whys[0] says level 1 is Ambessa's ("your Q cone's doubled outer edge beats his bare alternating-punch autos") but the chart gives it to Sett; whys[1] calls level 2 "genuinely even" but the chart gives it to Sett; whys[3] says "he owns levels 4-5" but the chart says Skill; whys[5] says "he keeps the edge" at first item but the chart says Skill.
audit.why: The packet levelChart (Ambessa, Skill, Sett, Sett, Sett, Sett, Skill) matches the prose exactly and matches the win rate: Ambessa's one clean window is level 1 before Grit and Facebreaker exist, then Sett owns the middle of the lane, then it evens out. A 46.24% lane that the text describes as his from 3 through first item is not a 6/10.
audit.corrected: diffRating raised to 7/10 and the Final Matchup Rating row updated to match. The side flips could not be applied — "Sett" is 4 characters, "Skill" 5 and "Ambessa" 7, so every swap crosses the length band. Documented in notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[1].why repeats the champion-wide "Dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade" error, and neither layer carries a single cooldown number.
audit.why: Drakehound's Step grants no shield. And the spike shape is entirely cooldown-driven: Haymaker 18s at rank 1, Facebreaker 16s, Knuckle Down 9s, The Show Stopper 120s. Facebreaker's 16s is the gap the reader is being told to punish and the number was never given.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why corrected; numbers written into spikes[1], mid, wants.you[1], breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1], dosFull[2] and all three dontsFull descriptions are stock boilerplate unrelated to their titles; the three don't-strings also form report[11].
audit.why: Each has a concrete answer here: the centre of Haymaker is the true-damage part, Grit is stored from damage he takes, and Facebreaker's stun needs enemies on both sides.
audit.corrected: All five rewritten against the kit.

notes:
The Facebreaker one-side rule is the highest-value thing in this file. Riot's text says plainly that enemies on only one side are slowed rather than stunned, which means in a 1v1 lane the stun is opt-in by positioning — and the entry told the reader eight separate times that it simply stuns. Everything downstream of that (when to step up, when to dash, whether Haymaker can be set up on you) was being taught off the wrong premise.

PACKET FALSE POSITIVE: suspectNames flags "Show Stopper" in spikes[2] against "the show stopper" at distance 4. The ability name is correct; the distance is entirely the missing article.

DIFFICULTY LABEL, partially fixed: diffRating is now 7/10 and the Final Matchup Rating row matches, but the diff field still reads "EVEN" at a 46.24% win rate in a lane the text hands to Sett from level 3 through first item. The vocabulary in this file is EVEN / TRICKY / HARD / FAV / MIRROR, and "EVEN" (4 characters) to "TRICKY" (6) crosses the band, so the label needs changing by hand. Worth noting for consistency: Poppy sits at TRICKY 7.5/10 on a 45.6% win rate, so Sett at EVEN was out of line with the champion's own scale.
